title_or_table: S. 146, TAKE IT DOWN Act, 119th Congress, actions (Library of Congress summary actions)
universe_or_base: The actions the Library of Congress records as the bill's major steps
vintage: Congress.gov data as served on November 11, 2026
qualification: The bill passed the Senate by unanimous consent with no recorded vote, and the House 409 to 2 under a suspension of the rules, which needs two-thirds; it became Public Law 119-12 on May 19, 2025
printed_source_line: Source: Library of Congress, Congress.gov, S. 146, TAKE IT DOWN Act, actions, January 16 to May 19, 2025, United States Congress. Retrieved November 11, 2026. Passed the Senate by unanimous consent with no recorded vote; became Public Law 119-12.
domain_note: The law requires online platforms to remove nonconsensual intimate images, including computer-made fakes, within 48 hours of a valid request; V7 places platforms and fake media under news, records and public information (issue I010)
notes: Hearing check, read November 12, 2026 (maker A’s R-A1, for S62): Congress.gov’s full action list for S. 146 (23 actions, api.congress.gov v3 /bill/119/s/146/actions) and its committees record (/committees) show the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation with two activities only, Referred To (January 16, 2025) and Discharged From (February 13, 2025, by unanimous consent); no hearing or markup is recorded. The House received S. 146 and held it at the desk (February 14, 2025), then passed it under suspension of the rules on April 28, 2025, with no committee referral. The committee’s own hearings list (commerce.senate.gov/hearings, all 24 pages of the 240 most recent meetings, 99 of them in the 119th Congress from January 15, 2025) names no hearing on the bill or its subject. The House companion, H.R. 633, has its own record: House Energy and Commerce marked it up on April 8, 2025 and reported it on April 28, 2025 (House Report 119-82, as the public law’s legislative history lists it)
